topic: The Solar System and Planetary Orbits
key_concepts: Typical grade-school solar system diagrams are often not to scale and omit objects.
Planetary orbits are elliptical in shape.
An ellipse can be modeled using two fixed points called foci and a loop of string.
Eccentricity describes the shape of an orbit.
Eccentricity is calculated by dividing the distance between foci by the major axis length.
Changing the distance between foci changes the eccentricity of an ellipse.
Changing the string length changes the size and shape of the constructed ellipse.
The Sun is located at one focus of a planet's elliptical orbit.
Earth's orbit has a low eccentricity and is nearly circular.
